context: batch chemical plant · solvent tank farm, hazardous-area electrics and fire protection govern

brief.intro: New to this project type? A paint factory is a batch chemical plant. Pigments and powders are dispersed into resin and solvent (or water) in high-speed mixers, ground fine in bead mills, 'let down' with more resin and additives in larger tanks, tinted to the right colour, filtered and filled into cans, pails and drums. Resins and solvents arrive by tanker and are stored in a tank farm, then piped to the production building. If the paints are solvent-based, the whole factory is a flammable-liquid site: the tank farm is bunded, the electrical equipment in production areas must be explosion-proof, everything is earthed against static sparks, ventilation is designed for vapours, and foam or sprinkler fire protection is extensive. Those safety systems — and the authority's approval of them — shape both design and schedule.

scope.desc: Portal frames, crane beams, roof and wall cladding, making the hall weather-tight.

scope.name: Filtration & filling
scope.desc: Filters, automatic filling, labelling and palletising lines.

scope.desc: Solvent & resin transfer piping, Compressed air & nitrogen blanketing, Chilled water for mills, Vapour extraction & dust collection — the services every machine needs before it can run.

scope.name: Power supply & control
scope.desc: Substation, transformers, switchgear, cabling and the plant control system.

scope.name: Fire protection, HVAC & dust / fume extraction
scope.desc: Life-safety and environmental systems required for the operating permit.

scope.name: Commissioning & ramp-up
scope.desc: Water or solvent trials of each line, first batches, colour and quality approval, then product-by-product ramp-up.

must_get_right: Get the hazardous-area classification and the fire strategy approved before detailed design — they decide the electrical equipment, ventilation, building separation and cost.
Explosion-proof equipment has long delivery and cannot be swapped for standard items; order it early and inspect its installation formally.
The fire-protection system (water tank, pumps, foam, sprinklers) must be accepted by the authority before flammable liquids are brought on site.
Earthing and bonding of every tank, pipe and filling point is a commissioning deliverable with records, not a detail.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities are organised by plant area along the process line and by discipline, with every long-lead machine tracked from order to factory test, shipping and arrival.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Standard site calendar for construction; equipment installation may run extended shifts under vendor supervision. Commissioning follows the vendor's programme, and hot commissioning runs continuously once started.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Hazardous-area and fire design approved → foundations, bunds and building → tanks, vessels and platforms → piping → Ex electrical installation → fire protection complete and accepted → leak tests and earthing checks → water trials → first solvent on site → first batches. The critical path runs through the fire-protection approval or the Ex equipment.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: The process technology and vendor are fixed before design starts; vendor drawings for foundations arrive on the agreed dates; permanent power and water are available before cold commissioning; raw material for trial production is on site.

sections.heading: Procurement & long-lead items
sections.body: The schedule tracks the following as milestones because they drive the programme:

rows: Before electrical installation in Ex areas

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Heavy machines need crane access and often must enter before the cladding or a wall is closed. Vendor supervisors are booked for fixed periods. Clean, dry, powered conditions are required before precision equipment is unpacked.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Main risks: late authority approval of the fire strategy, Ex equipment delivery, pipework leaks, and a failed fire-system acceptance delaying the first solvent delivery. Contingency is held before first batch.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 by plant area and discipline; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the installation crews and the vendor supervisors — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
